thesis: Corvane proposes accelerating growth by launching a paid Pro membership, adding AI reordering, and hiring 20 inside sales reps to transition contractor purchasing online.

assumptions.claim: Target contractor accounts are willing to pay an ongoing monthly subscription fee for guaranteed delivery and pricing.
assumptions.quote: 38% said they would pay a monthly fee to guarantee it.

test.method: Call 40 top-500 accounts offering early binding sign-up to Corvane Pro at $49 per month with standard payment terms.
test.metric: Number of accounts signing a paid enrollment agreement

assumptions.claim: Historical ERP transaction logs are sufficiently structured and accurate to train automated reorder algorithms immediately.
assumptions.quote: Our ERP order history is clean enough to train demand forecasts that predict what each contractor will need next week.

test.method: Audit a random sample of 300 contractor order histories across the past 24 months for SKU validity and catalog duplication.
test.metric: Percentage of historical order line items with validated, unambiguous product records

assumptions.claim: Executive leadership will authorize expanding the inside-sales team by 20 headcount in Q1.
assumptions.quote: Approve the Pro pricing and the Q1 hiring plan at the next leadership meeting.

test.method: Submit a formal hiring exception memo for 20 sales requisitions to executive leadership for sign-off.
test.metric: Number of approved new sales requisitions

assumptions.claim: The existing IT team has bandwidth to develop predictive reordering models concurrently with active IT projects.
assumptions.quote: Start the reorder-model build with the existing IT team.

test.method: Conduct an engineering capacity audit of the 4-person IT team against existing project roadmaps for the upcoming quarter.
test.metric: Unallocated weekly IT engineering hours available for model development

assumptions.claim: Sales reps will actively promote and migrate accounts to digital ordering despite earning commissions exclusively on self-placed orders.
assumptions.quote: Reps are the fastest path to adoption because contractors trust their branch contacts.

test.method: Survey all 35 inside-sales reps anonymously on whether they would pitch online ordering under current commission rules.
test.metric: Percentage of reps willing to actively onboard clients to online ordering without commission parity

assumptions.claim: Contractors are willing to abandon phone and counter ordering in favor of self-service digital workflows.
assumptions.quote: Corvane's contractors are ready to move ordering online, and the company that captures that shift first will own the regional market.

test.method: Send direct invitations for online ordering setup to 100 active contractors who routinely place orders via phone or counter.
test.metric: Percentage of invited contractors placing their next routine order via the web portal

assumptions.claim: National competitors will not offer local same-day delivery in Corvane's operating markets within the next 12 months.
assumptions.quote: national players have not yet built local same-day delivery, and they will not respond within the next 12 months.

test.method: Mystery-shop and interview local dispatch personnel across the top 3 national competitor distribution centers in Corvane's core region.
test.metric: Number of competitor branches offering or actively piloting local same-day jobsite delivery
test.go_if: 0 competitor branches offering or piloting same-day delivery
test.kill_if: >= 2 competitor branches offering or piloting same-day delivery

assumptions.claim: Gross margin will expand from 22% to 26% within 18 months through self-service order adoption and subscription fees.
assumptions.quote: gross margin rises from 22% to 26% within 18 months, driven by lower cost-to-serve and Pro membership fees.

test.method: Build an order-level unit economics model recalculating true gross margin across the two branch digital trials after factoring in free next-day delivery costs and bulk discounts.
test.metric: Net realized gross margin percentage on digital trial orders

conflicts.tension: Growth relies on hiring 20 inside-sales reps in Q1, but workforce policy mandates a strict hiring freeze that reduces inside-sales headcount.
conflicts.quote_b: A hiring freeze holds through the end of next fiscal year.

conflicts.tension: Growth plans to start building reorder models immediately with the existing IT team, but IT is fully committed to an ERP upgrade through Q3.
conflicts.quote_a: Start the reorder-model build with the existing IT team.
conflicts.quote_b: IT is fully committed to the ERP upgrade until Q3.

conflicts.tension: Growth asserts order history is clean enough for predictive modeling, while IT has found widespread duplicate and mislabeled records across historical orders.
conflicts.quote_a: Our ERP order history is clean enough to train demand forecasts that predict what each contractor will need next week.
conflicts.quote_b: the team has flagged duplicate and mislabeled product codes in roughly a fifth of historical orders.

conflicts.tension: Growth relies on sales reps to drive digital adoption, but current commission rules eliminate rep earnings on orders placed online.
conflicts.quote_a: Reps are the fastest path to adoption because contractors trust their branch contacts.
conflicts.quote_b: Orders that customers place online earn reps nothing.

conflicts.tension: Growth assumes contractors are ready to transition to online ordering, while customer survey data shows an overwhelming preference for phone and counter ordering to prevent order errors.
conflicts.quote_a: Corvane's contractors are ready to move ordering online, and the company that captures that shift first will own the regional market.
conflicts.quote_b: 41 of 50 contractors said they prefer to order by phone or at the counter, mostly because they rely on branch staff to catch mistakes in their orders.
